content:
The molecule is in its ground state (v=0, J=0). The next state with the lowest possible energy is the first vibrationally excited state (v=1, J=0 or J=1 depending on selection rules). The energy difference is dominated by the vibrational transition energy \(\Delta E = \hbar \omega\), since the rotational energy spacing is much smaller. The photon momentum is \(p = \Delta E / c\).

Given:
- \(\omega = 4 \times 10^{14} \, \text{rad/s}\)
- \(\hbar = 1.0546 \times 10^{-34} \, \text{J·s}\)
- \(c = 3.0 \times 10^8 \, \text{m/s}\)

\(\Delta E = \hbar \omega = (1.0546 \times 10^{-34})(4 \times 10^{14}) = 4.218 \times 10^{-20} \, \text{J}\)
\(p = \frac{4.218 \times 10^{-20}}{3.0 \times 10^8} = 1.406 \times 10^{-28} \, \text{N·s}\)

This matches option (B).

Answer: B
